problems.name: Sort Colors
problems.question: Given an array nums containing only 0, 1, and 2, sort it in-place so equal colors are grouped in the order 0, 1, 2.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 300; nums[i] is 0, 1, or 2; mutate nums in-place.

examples.explanation: All 0s move left and all 2s move right.
One pass partitions three values.
Middle values stay in the unknown scan zone until consumed.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). Dutch national flag partition scans each index at most once.

problems.name: Merge Sorted Array
problems.question: Given sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 where nums1 has enough trailing space, merge nums2 into nums1 as one sorted array.
problems.constraints: nums1.length == m + n; nums2.length == n; 0 <= m,n <= 200; mutate nums1.

examples.explanation: The arrays merge into one sorted sequence.
No second array values need to be copied.
The destination initially contains only buffer space.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(m+n); Space O(1). Merge from the back using three pointers.

problems.name: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.question: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array.

examples.explanation: The sorted order is [1,2,3,4,5,6].
Duplicates count as separate elements.
The only element is the first largest.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Average Time O(n), worst O(n^2); Space O(1). Iterative quickselect partitions in-place.

source.label: Kth Largest Element in an Array - LeetCode 215

problems.name: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.question: Given an integer array nums and integer k, return any order of the k most frequent elements.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 100000; k is in range [1, number of unique values].

examples.explanation: 1 appears three times and 2 appears twice.
Only one unique value exists.
4 and 6 tie for highest frequency.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n + u); Space O(n + u). Frequency buckets avoid sorting unique values.

problems.name: Largest Number
problems.question: Given a list of non-negative integers, arrange them so they form the largest possible number as a string.

examples.explanation: 2 before 10 makes 210 larger than 102.
Pairwise concatenation decides the custom order.
Leading zeros collapse to one zero.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n * d); Space O(n*d). Sort string forms by a+b versus b+a.

problems.name: Meeting Rooms
problems.question: Given meeting time intervals, return true if one person can attend all meetings.

examples.explanation: The meeting starting at 5 overlaps [0,30].
After sorting, 4 <= 7 so there is no overlap.
Touching endpoints do not overlap.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(log n). Sort by start and scan adjacent intervals.

problems.name: Meeting Rooms II
problems.question: Given meeting time intervals, return the minimum number of conference rooms required.

examples.explanation: At most two meetings overlap.
Meetings do not overlap.
All three overlap around time 3.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(n). Sort starts and ends, then sweep with two pointers.

problems.name: Merge Intervals
problems.question: Given intervals, merge all overlapping intervals and return the non-overlapping result.

examples.explanation: [1,3] overlaps [2,6].
Touching intervals merge.
Sorting places disjoint intervals in output order.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(n). Sort by start and scan once.

problems.name: Non-overlapping Intervals
problems.question: Given intervals, return the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest are non-overlapping.

examples.explanation: Remove [1,3].
Only one duplicate interval can remain.
Touching endpoints do not overlap.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(log n). Sort by end and greedily keep compatible intervals.

problems.name: H-Index
problems.question: Given citations where citations[i] is citations for a paper, return the researcher h-index.

examples.explanation: Three papers have at least three citations.
Only one paper has at least one citation after thresholding.
No paper has at least one citation.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Bucket citation counts capped at n.

problems.name: Wiggle Sort
problems.question: Given an unsorted array nums, reorder it in-place so nums[0] <= nums[1] >= nums[2] <= nums[3] and so on.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 50000; values fit in 32-bit signed integer; any valid wiggle order is accepted.

examples.output: a valid wiggle order such as [3,5,1,6,2,4]
examples.explanation: Every odd index is at least its neighbors.
Only adjacent wiggle inequalities must hold.
Equal values satisfy non-strict inequalities.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(1). One pass fixes each local violation by swapping adjacent values.

problems.name: Wiggle Sort II
problems.question: Given nums, reorder it in-place so nums[0] < nums[1] > nums[2] < nums[3] and so on.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 50000; a valid answer is guaranteed for the input.

examples.explanation: Odd indices are local peaks.
Duplicates are separated around peaks.
The median split prevents equal neighbors where possible.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Average Time O(n), worst O(n^2); Space O(1). Quickselect median, then virtual-index 3-way partition.

problems.name: Sort List
problems.question: Given the head of a linked list, sort the list in ascending order and return the sorted head.

examples.explanation: Merge sort orders the linked nodes.
Negative and positive values are both sorted.
An empty list stays empty.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(1) extra links. Bottom-up merge sort relinks nodes iteratively.

problems.name: Insertion Sort List
problems.question: Given the head of a linked list, sort it using insertion sort and return the sorted head.

examples.explanation: Each node is inserted into the sorted prefix.
Nodes are re-linked in ascending order.
A single node is already sorted.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(1). Insert each node into a sorted linked prefix.

problems.name: Relative Sort Array
problems.question: Given arr1 and arr2 where arr2 has distinct values appearing in arr1, sort arr1 so values in arr2 appear first in arr2 order and remaining values appear ascending.
problems.constraints: 1 <= arr1.length, arr2.length <= 1000; 0 <= arr1[i], arr2[i] <= 1000; arr2 values are distinct.

examples.explanation: Reference values come first in arr2 order.
Leftovers 17 and 44 are ascending.
Repeated reference values are emitted together.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n + range); Space O(range). Count values in the bounded domain and emit in required order.

problems.name: Sort Characters By Frequency
problems.question: Given a string s, sort its characters in decreasing frequency and return the resulting string.
problems.constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 500000; s contains uppercase/lowercase English letters and digits.

examples.explanation: e appears twice and comes first.
c and a tie, so either order is valid.
Uppercase and lowercase are different characters.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n + u); Space O(n + u). Bucket characters by frequency.

problems.name: Maximum Gap
problems.question: Given an integer array nums, return the maximum difference between two successive elements in sorted order.
problems.constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 100000; 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000; target linear time and space.

examples.explanation: Sorted order is [1,3,6,9], max gap is 3.
No adjacent pair exists.
The only sorted gap is the answer.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n); Space O(n). Use min/max buckets sized by pigeonhole lower bound.

problems.name: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
problems.question: Given nums, return counts where counts[i] is the number of smaller elements to the right of nums[i].

examples.explanation: 5 has smaller values 2 and 1 after it.
No values appear after the only element.
Equal values are not smaller.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(n). Fenwick tree over coordinate-compressed values scans from right.

source.label: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self - LeetCode 315

problems.name: Reverse Pairs
problems.question: Given nums, return the number of reverse pairs where i < j and nums[i] > 2 * nums[j].

examples.explanation: The reverse pairs are formed by values 3 with later 1s.
Three pairs satisfy nums[i] > 2*nums[j].
-5 > 2*(-5) is true for the first value before the second.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n log n); Space O(n). Fenwick tree with compressed values counts prior values greater than 2*x.

problems.name: Queue Reconstruction by Height
problems.question: Given people as [height, k], reconstruct the queue where k is the number of people in front with height at least height.

examples.explanation: Each person has exactly k taller-or-equal people before them.
Taller-first insertion satisfies all counts.
A single person is already valid.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2 + n log n); Space O(n). Sort by height descending/k ascending and insert at k.
